notes.meaning: Wisdom calls out openly so everyone can hear her. Unlike the deceitful woman in the previous chapter who whispers in dark corners, wisdom speaks publicly in broad daylight. She wants everyone to know the truth and avoid ruin.

Wisdom stands on high places along the road and right where different paths cross. She puts herself where travelers often get confused and need guidance. There she points people in the right direction before they make a wrong turn.

Wisdom takes her stand at the entrance of the city gates. These gates were the busiest spots in town, where courts met and crowds passed every day. She offers her advice where normal life happens so no one has an excuse for missing it.

Wisdom speaks to all human beings without favoritism. She calls out to leaders and nobles as well as to everyday laborers and the poor. Her message of salvation is offered freely to the entire human race.

Wisdom invites naive and inexperienced people to develop good judgment. She also urges stubborn fools to open their hearts and gain real understanding. No matter how ignorant someone has been, wisdom is ready to teach anyone willing to learn.

Wisdom promises that the things she teaches are noble, excellent, and trustworthy. She does not waste time with worthless or harmful gossip. Everything she shares is upright and helps people live straight, honest lives.
Wisdom always speaks the pure truth without any deceit. Wickedness, especially lying, is completely disgusting to her. Because she comes from God, her words can always be trusted.
All the teachings of wisdom are right, fair, and just. There is nothing twisted, tricky, or misleading in what she says. Her instructions never lead anyone into a moral trap.

God's truth is plain and easy to grasp for those who sincerely want to understand it. When a person is humble and willing to obey, the message becomes clear. The difficulty usually lies in stubborn hearts rather than in confusing words.

People are urged to choose godly instruction over piles of silver and choice gold. While money can only buy physical things, wisdom trains the soul for eternity. Knowing God is worth far more than material wealth.
Wisdom is more precious than the rarest jewels. Nothing in the entire world that a person could wish for compares to her value. Having earthly riches without wisdom only leads to misery.

Wisdom makes her home with prudence, which means using good sense in daily actions. She helps people invent good plans and make careful choices to avoid danger. True wisdom is practical and shapes how a person acts every day.

Reverence for the Lord means having a deep hatred for everything evil. Wisdom completely detests selfish pride, bad behavior, and crooked speech. You cannot love God while clinging to the sins that break His heart.

Wisdom possesses sound advice, deep insight, and the strength to carry out what is right. She does not just show people what to do; she provides the moral power needed to do it. Leaning on her guidance brings real stability in hard times.

Kings, princes, and judges are only able to govern properly through divine wisdom. Civil government is established by God, and rulers need His insight to make fair and righteous laws. When leaders ignore wisdom, their rule becomes cruel and corrupt.

Wisdom warmly welcomes all who love her, meeting their love with her own blessings. Those who search for her diligently, especially in their youth, are sure to find her. God never turns away anyone who seeks His guidance with an honest heart.

Wisdom brings true honor and lasting wealth that will not quickly vanish. While she often provides earthly stability, her greatest gifts are righteousness and peace with God. These spiritual treasures remain long after worldly fortunes are gone.

The harvest produced by wisdom is better than refined gold and choice silver. Earthly wealth can be stolen or lost, but the spiritual fruits of wisdom last forever. Investing your life in God's truth brings the greatest possible reward.

Wisdom walks firmly along the path of righteousness and stays centered in justice. She keeps her followers from straying into harmful extremes on either side. Living by her guidance keeps you safe from moral disaster.

Wisdom gives real, enduring substance to those who love her and fills their lives with true blessings. Earthly riches are often empty shadows, but God's gifts bring deep, lasting satisfaction. She ensures that her followers have an eternal inheritance.

The Lord possessed wisdom from the very beginning, before He made any of His ancient works. Wisdom was present with God before the universe was formed and shared in all His eternal plans. She is not a late addition to creation, but stands at the very start of God's ways.

differ.view: Wisdom here is Jesus Christ, the eternal Son of God, who was with the Father before time began and shares His divine nature.
This passage is a poetic personification of God's divine attribute of wisdom, not a direct statement about the eternal Sonship of Christ.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Wisdom is described as a divine figure or principle brought forth before creation to act as God's instrument in forming the universe.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The term 'possessed' shows that Christ is co-eternal with the Father, while ancient translations that read 'created' are understood as pointing to Christ taking on a human body in the Incarnation.

notes.meaning: Wisdom was appointed and established from eternity, long before the earth ever existed. Before time began, God's wise purpose was already determined. This shows that the principles of God's wisdom are timeless and unchanging.

Wisdom was brought forth before there were any deep oceans or overflowing springs. Long before waters covered the planet, wisdom had her being with God. Everything fluid and deep was planned by wisdom first.

Before the great mountains were settled into their rocky foundations, wisdom was already there. Even the oldest hills are young compared to God's eternal wisdom. Her existence reaches back further than the most solid parts of the earth.

Wisdom was present before God formed the dry land, open fields, or even the first speck of dust. The entire physical world was designed after wisdom was already established. Material things had a beginning, but wisdom predated them all.

When God spread out the heavens and carved out the horizon across the deep waters, wisdom was right beside Him. She was there when the universe received its boundaries and structure. The beauty of the sky shows the careful craftsmanship of God's wisdom.

Wisdom was there when God placed the clouds firmly in the sky above and secured the underground springs. He balanced the waters in the air and the waters beneath the earth. Nature holds together because it was designed with perfect skill.

Wisdom watched as God set limits for the oceans so the waters would not flood the land beyond His command. She was present when the solid foundations of the earth were laid down. The powerful forces of nature remain obedient to God's wise decree.

Wisdom was beside the Lord as a skilled master builder, rejoicing continually in His presence. God took daily delight in wisdom as the creation unfolded, and wisdom rejoiced back before Him. There was complete joy between the Creator and His wisdom as the universe was formed.

Wisdom took special pleasure in the inhabited earth and delighted particularly in human beings. God's wisdom is not distant or uncaring; she loves people and desires to fellowship with them. From the very start, humanity was the focus of God's loving wisdom.

Because wisdom is so ancient, divine, and loving, she urges everyone to listen to her words like obedient children. Those who carefully keep her ways will experience true happiness and blessing. Listening to God's wisdom is the only path to genuine peace.

Wisdom commands people to listen to discipline and instruction so they can become truly wise. Pushing away godly correction is foolish and dangerous. Welcoming instruction even when it corrects you is the mark of good sense.

A person is deeply blessed when they listen eagerly to wisdom every day, watching at her doors like an excited student. They do not treat God's truth as an occasional interest, but wait on Him regularly. Constant attention to God brings steady spiritual growth.

Whoever finds wisdom finds true spiritual life and receives the favor of the Lord. Knowing God's wisdom brings vitality to the soul and secures His loving approval. Finding wisdom is finding the true purpose of living.

Those who miss wisdom or sin against her bring terrible harm to their own souls. Rejecting God's truth is the same as choosing death, because sin naturally leads to destruction. People who turn away from wisdom destroy themselves by their own choice.
